content:
I was wondering if web pages created using Verso currently have support for displaying the general contents of the infoview. The use case I had in mind was to write a tutorial on widgets, for which it would be convenient if it were possible to render the JavaScript associated with a widget in the generated web page.

I imagine this might involve looking through the UserWidgetInfo nodes of the InfoTree, extracting their associated JavaScript content and somehow including this into the generated HTML output file. But as I write this, I realize that supporting general widgets in the web output may not be possible without a running Lean server instance, since widgets are allowed to call Lean functions via RPC.

I'd still be interested in hearing about the extent to which this would be possible to support and any suggestions on writing a widget-based tutorial using Verso. Thank you very much.

Hi @Anand Rao Tadipatri TTBOMK Verso and Widgets don't have this functionality yet, but it is something that we have discussed internally in the FRO a few times, and in the issue tracker https://github.com/leanprover/verso/issues/311

Thanks for your interest @Anand Rao Tadipatri ! The 2nd item in the issue Emilio linked partly addresses your question of widgets being allowed to call Lean via RPC. My hope (untested) is that providing a fake RPC server in Verso-webpages would get us part of the way there; widgets that really do rely on RPC will not work, but many widgets show something useful even when RPC isn't working (e.g. the Lean server died). We should eventually make all of this explicit in @leanprover/infoview, but trying out such a setup would provide a useful datapoint, if you were so inclined.

Thank you both for your responses! I wonder if it might be possible to automatically embed an iframe pointing to live.lean-lang.org with the relevant code loaded at every point in the file where a UserWidgetInfo is detected. It's not clear at all to me whether this kind of thing is doable and how it would work, but I think it would be nice if such a set-up allowed one to then demostrate widgets that rely on RPC.

Actually, for the purpose of writing a Verso document showcasing some widgets, it might be sufficient to have a way of configuring a code block to be displayed as an embedded live.lean-lang.org page instead of in the usual Verso style.

automatically embed an iframe pointing to live.lean-lang.org with the relevant code loaded at every point in the file where a UserWidgetInfo is detected

If you literally did that, it may lead to spawning #(UserWidgetInfo) Lean servers in the backend that live.lean-lang.org connects to. On the whole, I would see displaying only the static parts of widgets as more promising for archival-style artifacts (reference manuals, textbooks, ..), and the RPC-aware parts as something confined to editor-like environments. I am happy to be convinced otherwise, though :)

Apologies for the delay in responding. I think it would be nice to be able to display both static and dynamic widgets in a tutorial on widgets, if that's feasible.

For the static ones (or ones for which the dynamic content is not crucial for the explanation), I'd be in favour of the approach you proposed of creating a custom JavaScript environment for displaying the static parts of widgets directly in the Verso web page.

For situations where dynamic behaviour relying on RPC is necessary for the explanation, rather than linking to live.lean-lang.org pages on a Verso web page I feel that it might be convenient to have a way to configure a Verso code block to have it show up as an embedded iframe pointing to a live.lean-lang.org page with the relevant code, if that's possible.

Since this is not meant to be a standalone but a part of a broader tutorial on using Lean, I'd prefer to use Verso instead of creating a repository for the tutorial that's meant to be run in the editor (which otherwise might not have been a bad option, given that it it involves a bit of communicating the Lean server). I'd be interested in hearing your thoughts on this.

Ah, so these are really two separate feature requests. One is to display widgets in some form without a Lean server in rendered Verso contents, the other is to

configure a Verso code block to have it show up as an embedded iframe pointing to a live.lean-lang.org page with the relevant code, if that's possible.

We currently have Live links that open up a new tab. You are asking if the tab could show up as an inline iframe instead. There are some UX issues to solve, e.g. one probably shouldn't show the top bar with the hamburger menu in this case. This is a mild change - whether readers have to switch to a new tab or not - so I imagine it would not be high priority and - fair warning - may even be a not planned, but you could write an RFC.

Thank you for letting me know about Live links, I was certain that a feature like that must exist but I wasn't sure what it was called. They might be good enough for my immediate purposes.
Another UX/editor feature that would be nice to have, but not essential for a first version is the ability to "gray out" or collapse an initial segment of the code in the file that is necessary for the code below to compile but not directly relevant to the actual demonstration.
I'll plan to write up an RFC soon, thank you for the suggestion.

You can also implement these things yourself for your own project to gain experience with them. Verso code is just Lean code, and you can implement whatever library you need. That can be a good way to figure out what actually works well in practice, which sometimes takes some experimentation. An RFC will be more convincing if it's accompanied by a working prototype that has delivered real value. And you may discover that your needs are specific enough that it makes more sense to upstream just some reusable library code. Give it a go!
Thanks, that sounds like a good idea!
